text.p: The Estonian economy grew by 3.5 percent during the first nine months of the year compared to the same period last year, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
It said in a report on the economic situation that service industries grew over the first three quarters but processing industries stagnated.
"Estonian economic growth continued in the third quarter," the ministry said.

"The first nine month results of 1996 compared to the first nine month results of 1995 show an increase of 3.5 pct in GDP (gross domestic product), taking into account price increases," the ministry added.
It said that GDP came to 38 billion kroons after three quarters, including 14 billion kroons in the third quarter.
Estimates for total year growth in Estonia have ranged between two and three percent.
